reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: D gives v = 2t − 5 and s = t² − 5t + 11 in SI units when t is the numerical time in seconds. These agree with the shifted-time laws and both initial values. The reversal occurs at 2.5 s and 4.75 m. The next positions are 5.00 and 7.00 m. The acceleration area is +4 m/s. The signed velocity triangles are −½(0.5)(1) = −0.25 m and +½(1.5)(3) = +2.25 m, giving +2.00 m displacement and 2.50 m distance. The prediction lies in [6.98, 7.08] m. Braking gives v = 6 − 2t and s = 6t − t², with a stop at 3 s and 9 m. Continuing to 5 s gives −4 m/s and 5 m. Remaining at rest gives zero velocity and acceleration at 9 m.
reviews.fullPreparationReview: The direct motion-laws goal prepares learners to relate graphs, laws and predictions. Its acceleration, signed-area, slope, function-value and geometry prerequisites supply the methods for both cases. The post-stop question can be answered by showing what continued negative acceleration does to a vehicle initially at rest. It requires no independent force calculation or general justification of idealizations.
reviews.directCoverageReview: The candidate directly tests the constant-acceleration goal through two sets of position, velocity and acceleration representations, the reversal, the area balance and the limit of the braking model. The broader motion-laws goal also includes deriving laws for uniform motion from diagrams. This task does not establish that whole goal.
reviews.falsePassCheck: Each of the four rows has a 2-point core and a maximum of 5. Missing any core caps the score at 1 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 16. Consequently 17/20 requires both sets of representations, a signed-area argument applied to the reversal, and a physical explanation of the invalid extension. Some numerical details can be missed at 17. The original had the same protection but could withhold a mark for a correct original-time solution.
reviews.languageReview: Both candidate keys show the signed arithmetic and both forms of the time laws. Both scoring texts now accept either time coordinate when the learner uses the initial conditions consistently. The German and English prompts also allow sufficiently precise descriptions of the graphs.
scopeLimitations: The log and check reading are supplied. The assessment establishes no personal measurement performance.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: D′ has the same correct kinematics in both versions. The positions are 4.75, 5.00 and 7.00 m, the velocity change is +4 m/s, and the signed areas give +2.00 m displacement over 2.50 m of travel. The independent check succeeds because |7.00 − 7.03| = 0.03 m ≤ 0.05 m. The brake model stops at 3 s and 9 m. Its extension gives −4 m/s and 5 m at 5 s. The supplied ±0.05 m defines a comparison interval. Its origin as an instrument resolution cannot be inferred.
reviews.fullPreparationReview: The motion-laws prerequisite and its graph, slope, signed-area, algebra and unit ancestry cover the task. Reading a supplied interval requires no independent uncertainty estimate. Explaining why the program predicts backward motion requires applying the velocity law beyond the stop and identifying the physical assumption that fails.
reviews.directCoverageReview: All five 4-point rows are required at 20/20. The graph construction, explanation of the areas and reversal, and application of the braking laws establish the constant-acceleration goal. The defect in row 3 affects the independent check. It does not remove the evidence for that goal.
reviews.falsePassCheck: Dropping a point in any row caps the total at 19. Nevertheless, the literal candidate row 3 asks the learner to compare the check mark with the supplied interval. Showing that 7.03 m lies inside its own interval satisfies that wording without ever testing the model prediction. The task and worked solution intend the scientifically meaningful comparison with 7.00 m.
reviews.languageReview: Both candidate prompts now explicitly request the program’s velocity and position at 5 s. Both first rows accept either time coordinate, correcting the original’s shifted-origin restriction. Both third rows replace the unsupported reference to resolution with an interval, but retain the same error about which quantity to compare.
requiredCorrections: Correct the comparison in acceleration-log_3 in both languages. For example, use ‘prüft, ob der vorhergesagte Ort bei 4 s im angegebenen Kontrollintervall liegt’ and ‘checks whether the predicted position at 4 s lies in the supplied check interval’. Retain the distinction between displacement and distance in that row.
scopeLimitations: The full-score rule guarantees the named rows. It cannot resolve an incorrectly worded criterion.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: NVX gives horizontal velocity 2.0 m/s at both instants and downward components 1.5 and 3.0 m/s. At the example scale the horizontal arrow is 4 cm and the downward arrows are 3 and 6 cm. The magnitudes are 2.5 m/s and √13 m/s ≈ 3.61 m/s. The impact angle is arctan(3/2) ≈ 56.31° below horizontal, within the 54°–58° drawing tolerance. The angle steepens as the downward component grows. In the cart frame the ball falls vertically and reaches 3.0 m/s downward. Adding the cart’s horizontal velocity recovers the ground-frame impact vector.
reviews.fullPreparationReview: The sole direct vector-velocity prerequisite includes horizontal projection and reference-frame superposition in its ancestry. Those branches supply free fall, uniform horizontal motion, component addition, scale constructions, angle measurement and Pythagoras. The measurement route makes trigonometric inversion optional.
reviews.directCoverageReview: The five rows require both pairs of components, their combination into two scaled resultants, both magnitudes, and direction through the impact angle and its change. This establishes all facets of VEC. The cart row also assesses relative velocity, but the task chooses the frames for the learner. Independent choice of a suitable frame is part of the reference-frame goal.
reviews.falsePassCheck: At the original 12/16 threshold, omitting the entire magnitude row still allowed 13, as did omitting the cart row. At 16/16 every row must be complete. In particular, the cart row requires the vertical-fall description, the 3.0 m/s downward relative velocity and the arrow addition. Carrying an error forward can preserve later method marks, but the lost component mark already prevents a pass.
reviews.languageReview: The original prompts and angle row called for measurement while the keys also allowed calculation. Both candidate prompts and the revised row now agree on the two valid routes and their expected results. The scaled vector constructions remain compulsory in both languages.
scopeLimitations: NVX has no guaranteed planning-credit target. The prescribed cart-frame exercise supports no whole BZ claim.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: DFD gives x/t = 2.0 m/s and downward distance divided by t² of 5.00, 5.00 and 4.89 m/s². The nearly constant latter ratio supports approximately quadratic fall over the sampled interval. Eliminating the shared time gives an approximately parabolic trajectory. Superproportional growth alone, as in the original key, is insufficient. At 50 and 100 km/h the one-second reaction distances are about 13.9 and 27.8 m. Adding the supplied 14 and 56 m gives 27.9 and 83.8 m, a ratio of about 3.004. This compares stopping clearances before a stationary obstacle. The two given braking distances are consistent with quadratic scaling under the same constant deceleration.
reviews.fullPreparationReview: Retain horizontal projection for the calibrated two-coordinate video analysis and trajectory, traffic for reaction and braking distances, and model limits for the transfer judgment. Their ancestry supplies free fall, motion laws, measurement scales, unit conversions and proportional comparisons. A moving lead vehicle would require other information. The clarified task needs none.
reviews.directCoverageReview: The traffic goal permits a stopped queue as an everyday safety-distance case. It also expressly requires qualitative and model-based assessment of reaction and braking distances. The exact candidate row requires using the given braking distances and judging the total clearance, but leaves qualitative interpretation of the two contributions optional. Traffic is the sole recommended claim after that repair. Part A describes an analysis of supplied coordinates. It does not require conducting the experiment or producing the full experimental horizontal-projection performance. Naming one limit likewise falls short of the whole idealizations goal.
reviews.falsePassCheck: The original 10/16 allowed an 8 + 2 split in either direction. At 16/16 the candidate requires both full rows. Row A jointly requires calibration and tracking of both coordinates, separate representations and a common-time justification of the parabola. In row B, a learner can show both reaction calculations, add 14 and 56 m, conclude ‘about three times’, and state ‘reaction times vary’. That earns every named contribution while leaving unexplained how the reaction and braking distances themselves change. The worked key cannot make an omitted scoring requirement compulsory.
reviews.languageReview: The original lacks an English task and key, and its German traffic row asks for calculation of braking distances that were supplied. The candidate provides parallel tasks, keys and conjunctive rows in both languages. Its unchanged English assessment description still promises a ‘safe following distance’, which conflicts with the expressly stationary obstacle.
requiredCorrections: Make the qualitative reasoning explicit in both versions of part B and its full-mark row. At fixed reaction time, doubling speed doubles reaction distance. The supplied braking distance quadruples. Require the learner to use that difference to explain the stopping-clearance judgment. The given numbers suffice without deriving a universal braking law.

Replace ‘safe following distance’ in descriptionEn with the required stopping clearance before a stationary obstacle. Align the worked explanations with the revised row and restore the missing spaces around numbers in the candidate prose.
scopeLimitations: The traffic coverage recommendation is conditional on the row repair. The supplied coordinates have no stated measurement-error bounds, and no video or personal observations were available for inspection.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: With downward positive, x = x₀ + v₀t + gt²/2. For a justified release from rest at the chosen origin, the slope of x against t² is g/2. A quadratic fit with checked initial conditions is valid for an evidenced nonzero v₀. Repeated releases inform scatter, while varying timing or reading limits tests sensitivity. A common calibration can affect both series. At g = 9.81 m/s², falls of 0.30 and 0.60 m take about 0.247 and 0.350 s, or about 30 and 42 frame intervals at 120 actual frames/s. These are feasibility calculations. Each reported experimental g must come from the learner’s own observations.
reviews.fullPreparationReview: FF expressly teaches experimental free fall near Earth, graphical analysis of measurements, determination of g in the model without air resistance, and a time-position law with initial conditions. Its direct parents are motion laws (262f807a-30d0-503e-986f-856cbd048e8e) and measurement uncertainty (f6b1d812-ce8b-5852-b417-e6c29b533c7a). The latter includes systematic and random deviations. The task supplies the fitting and sensitivity procedures. Its mandatory model judgment concerns what the learner’s two series support given release, timing, parallax and drag. No part requires choosing a point-particle representation, justifying neglected rotation or size, or independently selecting an idealization. There is no missing mandatory skill that warrants a separate MOD edge.
reviews.directCoverageReview: Each measured height requires at least three valid personal releases, at least five traceable time-position pairs per release, measured-point graphs, a graphical or justified quadratic determination of g, and a separate law with checked initial conditions. Both series require uncertainty analysis, and the final comparison requires a bounded quantitative interpretation. These performances directly establish FF. The comparison remains valid when the data cannot resolve a difference.
reviews.falsePassCheck: There are eight 3-point cores, four for each series. A missing central component earns zero for its core, capping the total at 21/24. A pass at 23 permits only one 2-point core, which must still be complete apart from an isolated nonconceptual slip. A plan, a reference value inserted as data, or a second law copied from the first series cannot satisfy this rule.
reviews.languageReview: The original German solution named the limits of the ‘Luftwiderstandsmodell’, while both tasks and the English key examine the model without air resistance. The candidate’s sole change corrects that scientific distinction. The personal-data requirements, alternative recording arrangements and grading rule agree across languages.
scopeLimitations: The practical requires an actual teacher-checked setup with suitable acquisition equipment. The supplied materials establish neither local availability nor experimental execution.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: ZB’s constructed values satisfy x = 2t, y = 1.25 − 5t², vᵧ = −10t and aᵧ = −10 in SI units. At 0.20 s the positions are 0.40 and 1.05 m. Both bodies reach the plane at 0.500 s. B travels 1.00 m and its signed impact components are +2.00 and −5.00 m/s. Eliminating time gives y = 1.25 m − (1.25 m⁻¹)x². Doubling horizontal speed gives 2.00 m at the same flight time. The drag reasoning is sound. A vertical drag component can depend on total speed, so equal arrival times cease to be guaranteed. Some drag models still give equal times. The numerical grading guidance, however, contains incompatible rounding instructions.
reviews.fullPreparationReview: Horizontal projection supplies simultaneous component motions, shared flight time and trajectory construction. Its free-fall and motion-law ancestry supplies the signed vertical laws and graphs. MOD, through its comparison of falls in air and vacuum, supplies the independent justification of the point-particle and negligible-drag assumptions and the limits of the predictions. This task expressly asks for that justification in part 6. It requires neither vector synthesis nor a quantitative drag law.
reviews.directCoverageReview: Criteria 6.1–6.6 require the purpose and suitable conditions of the point-particle approximation, the role of a uniform field, the consequences of negligible drag, and a reason the ideal equal-time prediction can fail. Earning all six establishes MOD. The projectile data are constructed and supply no personal experimental evidence for the whole horizontal-projection goal.
reviews.falsePassCheck: At the original 22/36, a learner could leave all of part 6 blank and earn 30. At the candidate’s native 36/36, every one-point criterion is necessary. Error carry-forward preserves appropriate later method marks and cannot replace independent physical explanations. The total therefore closes the MOD false-pass path without a separate runtime gate. A false failure remains possible: a learner can report the final trajectory coefficient 1.25 m⁻¹ as 1.3 m⁻¹ to two significant figures. This is valid rounding but differs by 4%, enough to lose the pass under the stated 1% cap.
reviews.languageReview: The German and English tasks, keys and individual criteria agree on the axes, signs, required graphs and qualitative treatment of drag. Both sets of marking principles accept sensible rounding to two or three significant figures and also impose the conflicting 1% tolerance. The same correction is needed in each.
requiredCorrections: Reconcile the bilingual marking principles so exact results and final values correctly rounded to the permitted precision earn full credit, including when correct rounding exceeds 1%. Retain unrounded intermediate values for subsequent calculations, the 36 individual criteria, equivalent physical arguments and the native 36/36 total.
scopeLimitations: A learner can demonstrate all of MOD and still miss the proposed assessment pass through another criterion. The guarantee runs from a valid pass to the required evidence. Its effect on learner outcomes has not been measured.

ffxHesseOfferReason: The official Hessen Kerncurriculum Physik, printed p. 30, places experimental data collection, graphical representation, determination of gravitational acceleration, discussion of deviation from a literature value, formulation of a mathematical model and determination of a time-position law under E.1 free fall. It lists point-particle and friction idealizations separately. The corrected FFX is compatible with a voluntary Hessen upper-secondary practical. FFX explicitly requires a quantitative A/B comparison but does not separately require a discussion of deviation from a literature value. The offer therefore supports the stated native FF goal without attesting every official subfacet. The supplied Hessen source does not independently validate the existing Saxony year-9 placement.
directCoverageVersusPlanningCredit: A recommended covered ID identifies the whole content goal evidenced by a passing performance under the stated rubric. For DFD the recommendation applies after the qualitative traffic criterion is repaired. A prerequisite records preparation for a demand. Neither relationship by itself grants planning credit, transfers a previous result or establishes individual mastery. NVX has no guaranteed planning-credit target, including VEC.
crossGoalFindings: D and D′ assess the same constant-acceleration goal through different score rules. D requires at least the conceptual core of every row at 17/20. D′ requires all five full rows at 20/20.

The D′ revision concerns the comparison quantity, the DFD revision concerns evidence missing from a full-mark row and its English description, and the ZB revision concerns rejection of correctly rounded physics. Raising a threshold addresses none of those wording defects.

FFX requires interpreting the limits of a named model against personal measurements. ZB explicitly requires justifying model idealizations. This difference supports retaining MOD as a direct prerequisite for ZB and sole direct FF for FFX. No prerequisite disagreement remains unresolved.
globalLimitations: These are proposals about the exact supplied texts. All six maxima, placements and the E.1 cut are preserved. No canonical file, historical evidence, previous learner result or V9 proof was changed.

No task images, learner responses, real measurements or host-equipment checks were supplied. The review establishes no learner difficulty calibration, pass rate, practical execution or official state-exam endorsement.
Materials, introductions, planning-credit byte seals and final status labels are outside this content review.
